document.description: LptA is an essential, signal-peptide-bearing periplasmic protein of the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia coli. Its mature chain folds into a twisted beta-jellyroll with a hydrophobic groove, and it binds LPS through the lipid A moiety. LptA docks by its N-terminal edge onto the C-terminal edge of the beta-jellyroll of the inner-membrane protein LptC, and by its C-terminal edge onto the N-terminal periplasmic domain of the outer-membrane translocon LptD. One or a few head-to-tail LptA molecules thereby complete a continuous trans-envelope protein bridge. LPS extracted from the inner membrane by the ATP-driven LptB2FG transporter is passed from LptC to LptA and along the bridge to LptDE, which inserts it into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. Bridge assembly is gated by correct LptDE assembly, and LptA is unstable when the bridge cannot form. Depletion of LptA blocks LPS delivery to the outer membrane, causes LPS to accumulate in the inner membrane and is lethal. Expression of the lptA-lptB operon is controlled by sigma-E.

document.description: LptB (formerly YhbG) is the nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) subunit of the LptB2FG ABC transporter of the Escherichia coli inner membrane. Two LptB copies form a homodimeric ATPase that sits on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane, docked onto the coupling helices of the transmembrane subunits LptF and LptG; the bitopic protein LptC associates with LptB2FG to form the LptB2FGC inner membrane complex. ATP binding and hydrolysis by LptB drive conformational changes in LptFG that extract newly synthesized lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane (after MsbA has flipped it) and push it into the periplasmic LptC-LptA-LptD protein bridge, which delivers LPS to the LptDE translocon for insertion into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. LptB is essential; its depletion or catalytic inactivation (E163Q) blocks LPS transport and outer membrane biogenesis. Unlike classical ABC transporters, LptB2FG does not move its substrate across the bilayer but extrudes it out of the membrane.

document.description: LptC (formerly YrbK) is an essential bitopic inner-membrane protein of the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia coli. It has a single N-terminal transmembrane helix and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain that resembles LptA. LptC forms a tight complex with the ABC transporter LptB2FG, inserting its transmembrane helix between the LptF and LptG transmembrane domains, where it modulates transporter ATPase activity. The N-terminal edge of its beta-jellyroll contacts the periplasmic beta-jellyrolls of LptF/LptG. LPS extracted from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane by ATP hydrolysis is passed into the LptC beta-jellyroll and then to LptA, which docks on the C-terminal edge of LptC. Transfer is unidirectional, as LptA can displace LPS from LptC but not the reverse. Through LptA, LptC links the inner-membrane extractor to the outer-membrane LptDE translocon in a continuous trans-envelope bridge. Depletion of LptC blocks LPS delivery to the outer membrane, causes envelope defects and is lethal.

document.description: LptD (formerly Imp/OstA) is an essential 87 kDa integral outer-membrane protein of Escherichia coli and the beta-barrel subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It has an N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain, of the same OstA fold as LptA and LptC, and a C-terminal 26-stranded beta-barrel, the two linked by two interdomain disulfide bonds (Cys31-Cys724 and Cys173-Cys725), at least one of which is needed for function. The outer-membrane lipoprotein LptE sits inside the barrel as a plug. The jellyroll domain docks the C-terminus of periplasmic LptA, completing the LptB2FGC-LptA-LptD protein bridge that spans the envelope and carries LPS from the inner membrane. Arriving LPS is thought to move its core oligosaccharide and O-antigen through the barrel lumen while lipid A enters the outer leaflet through a lateral gate between barrel strands 1 and 26. LptD is folded and inserted by the BAM complex with the help of SurA, Skp, DsbA, DsbC, BepA, LptE and the lipoprotein LptM. Partial loss of LptD increases outer-membrane permeability to detergents, antibiotics, dyes, large maltodextrins and n-hexane; depletion blocks delivery of new LPS to the cell surface and is lethal.

document.description: LptE (formerly RlpB, "rare lipoprotein B") is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein of Escherichia coli and the plug subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It is triacylated at its N-terminal cysteine and delivered to the inner leaflet of the outer membrane by the Lol pathway. About three quarters of LptE sits inside the lumen of the 26-stranded LptD beta-barrel, forming a two-protein plug-and-barrel complex in 1:1 stoichiometry. LptE has two roles. First, it is needed for LptD biogenesis: it engages LptD while BAM assembles it, stabilizes the barrel, and drives the disulfide rearrangement that yields functional, correctly oxidized LptD. Second, it binds LPS directly through conserved basic surface loops and can disrupt LPS-LPS interactions, which may help LPS insertion into the outer leaflet. Depletion of LptE stops newly made LPS from reaching the cell surface, raises outer-membrane permeability, and is lethal.

document.description: LptF (formerly YjgP) is an essential inner-membrane protein of Escherichia coli and one of the two paralogous transmembrane domain (TMD) subunits of the LptB2FG ATP-binding cassette transporter, which extracts lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the periplasmic (outer) leaflet of the inner membrane and starts its delivery to the outer membrane. LptF has six transmembrane helices with cytoplasmic N and C termini and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain between TM3 and TM4. Its transmembrane helices pair with those of LptG to form a V-shaped, outward-open hydrophobic cavity that receives LPS laterally from the membrane; Arg33 on TM1 of LptF contacts the phosphorylated inner core and is essential for viability. Exchange beta-jellyroll domains between LptF and LptG and test complementation of LptF/LptG depletion strains and LPS transport in reconstituted proteoliposomes to determine what role the LptG periplasmic domain plays, given that LptC docks on the LptF beta-jellyroll.

taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:83333
  label: Escherichia coli K-12
description: LptA is an essential, signal-peptide-bearing periplasmic protein of
  the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia
  coli. Its mature chain folds into a twisted beta-jellyroll with a hydrophobic
  groove, and it binds LPS through the lipid A moiety. LptA docks by its N-terminal
  edge onto the C-terminal edge of the beta-jellyroll of the inner-membrane protein
  LptC, and by its C-terminal edge onto the N-terminal periplasmic domain of the
  outer-membrane translocon LptD. One or a few head-to-tail LptA molecules thereby
  complete a continuous trans-envelope protein bridge. LPS extracted from the inner
  membrane by the ATP-driven LptB2FG transporter is passed from LptC to LptA and
  along the bridge to LptDE, which inserts it into the outer leaflet of the outer
  membrane. Bridge assembly is gated by correct LptDE assembly, and LptA is
  unstable when the bridge cannot form. Depletion of LptA blocks LPS delivery to
  the outer membrane, causes LPS to accumulate in the inner membrane and is lethal.
  Expression of the lptA-lptB operon is controlled by sigma-E.

description: LptB (formerly YhbG) is the nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) subunit
  of the LptB2FG ABC transporter of the Escherichia coli inner membrane. Two LptB
  copies form a homodimeric ATPase that sits on the cytoplasmic face of the inner
  membrane, docked onto the coupling helices of the transmembrane subunits LptF and
  LptG; the bitopic protein LptC associates with LptB2FG to form the LptB2FGC inner
  membrane complex. ATP binding and hydrolysis by LptB drive conformational changes
  in LptFG that extract newly synthesized lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer
  leaflet of the inner membrane (after MsbA has flipped it) and push it into the
  periplasmic LptC-LptA-LptD protein bridge, which delivers LPS to the LptDE
  translocon for insertion into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. LptB is
  essential; its depletion or catalytic inactivation (E163Q) blocks LPS transport
  and outer membrane biogenesis. Unlike classical ABC transporters, LptB2FG does not
  move its substrate across the bilayer but extrudes it out of the membrane.

description: LptC (formerly YrbK) is an essential bitopic inner-membrane protein
  of the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia
  coli. It has a single N-terminal transmembrane helix and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll
  domain that resembles LptA. LptC forms a tight complex with the ABC transporter
  LptB2FG, inserting its transmembrane helix between the LptF and LptG transmembrane
  domains, where it modulates transporter ATPase activity. The N-terminal edge of
  its beta-jellyroll contacts the periplasmic beta-jellyrolls of LptF/LptG. LPS
  extracted from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane by ATP hydrolysis is passed
  into the LptC beta-jellyroll and then to LptA, which docks on the C-terminal edge
  of LptC. Transfer is unidirectional, as LptA can displace LPS from LptC but not
  the reverse. Through LptA, LptC links the inner-membrane extractor to the outer-membrane
  LptDE translocon in a continuous trans-envelope bridge. Depletion of LptC blocks
  LPS delivery to the outer membrane, causes envelope defects and is lethal.

description: >-
  LptD (formerly Imp/OstA) is an essential 87 kDa integral outer-membrane protein
  of Escherichia coli and the beta-barrel subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide
  (LPS) translocon. It has an N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain, of the
  same OstA fold as LptA and LptC, and a C-terminal 26-stranded beta-barrel, the
  two linked by two interdomain disulfide bonds (Cys31-Cys724 and Cys173-Cys725),
  at least one of which is needed for function. The outer-membrane lipoprotein LptE
  sits inside the barrel as a plug. The jellyroll domain docks the C-terminus of
  periplasmic LptA, completing the LptB2FGC-LptA-LptD protein bridge that spans
  the envelope and carries LPS from the inner membrane. Arriving LPS is thought to
  move its core oligosaccharide and O-antigen through the barrel lumen while lipid A
  enters the outer leaflet through a lateral gate between barrel strands 1 and 26.
  LptD is folded and inserted by the BAM complex with the help of SurA, Skp, DsbA,
  DsbC, BepA, LptE and the lipoprotein LptM. Partial loss of LptD increases
  outer-membrane permeability to detergents, antibiotics, dyes, large maltodextrins
  and n-hexane; depletion blocks delivery of new LPS to the cell surface and is
  lethal.

description: >-
  LptE (formerly RlpB, "rare lipoprotein B") is an essential outer-membrane
  lipoprotein of Escherichia coli and the plug subunit of the LptDE
  lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It is triacylated at its N-terminal
  cysteine and delivered to the inner leaflet of the outer membrane by the Lol
  pathway. About three quarters of LptE sits inside the lumen of the 26-stranded
  LptD beta-barrel, forming a two-protein plug-and-barrel complex in 1:1
  stoichiometry. LptE has two roles. First, it is needed for LptD biogenesis: it
  engages LptD while BAM assembles it, stabilizes the barrel, and drives the
  disulfide rearrangement that yields functional, correctly oxidized LptD.
  Second, it binds LPS directly through conserved basic surface loops and can
  disrupt LPS-LPS interactions, which may help LPS insertion into the outer
  leaflet. Depletion of LptE stops newly made LPS from reaching the cell surface,
  raises outer-membrane permeability, and is lethal.

description: LptF (formerly YjgP) is an essential inner-membrane protein of
  Escherichia coli and one of the two paralogous transmembrane domain (TMD)
  subunits of the LptB2FG ATP-binding cassette transporter, which extracts
  lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the periplasmic (outer) leaflet of the inner
  membrane and starts its delivery to the outer membrane. LptF has six
  transmembrane helices with cytoplasmic N and C termini and a periplasmic
  beta-jellyroll domain between TM3 and TM4. Its transmembrane helices pair
  with those of LptG to form a V-shaped, outward-open hydrophobic cavity that
  receives LPS laterally from the membrane; Arg33 on TM1 of LptF contacts the
  phosphorylated inner core and is essential for viability. Coupling helices
  of LptF and LptG dock into the groove of the LptB ATPase dimer, linking ATP
  hydrolysis to cavity collapse and LPS expulsion. The transmembrane helix of
  LptC packs against TM5 of LptF, and the LptF beta-jellyroll domain binds the
  N-terminal end of the LptC beta-jellyroll, forming a continuous groove that
  begins the periplasmic LptC-LptA-LptD bridge through which LPS is pushed to
  the cell surface. Depletion of LptF blocks LPS transport, compromises the
  outer-membrane permeability barrier and arrests growth.

description: LptG (formerly YjgQ) is an essential inner-membrane protein of
  Escherichia coli and one of the two paralogous transmembrane domain (TMD)
  subunits of the LptB2FG ATP-binding cassette transporter, which extracts
  lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the periplasmic (outer) leaflet of the inner
  membrane and starts its delivery to the outer membrane. LptG has six
  transmembrane helices with cytoplasmic N and C termini and a periplasmic
  beta-jellyroll domain between TM3 and TM4. Its transmembrane helices pair
  with those of LptF to form a V-shaped, outward-open hydrophobic cavity that
  receives LPS laterally from the membrane; a cluster of lysine and arginine
  residues on TM1-TM3 of LptG binds the lipid A 1-phosphate, and Lys34 on TM1
  is essential for LPS transport and growth. Coupling helices of LptG and LptF
  dock into the groove of the LptB ATPase dimer, linking ATP hydrolysis to
  cavity collapse and LPS expulsion. The transmembrane helix of LptC wedges
  between TM1 of LptG and TM5 of LptF, holding the LptG helices apart and
  regulating LPS binding and ATPase activity. Depletion of LptG blocks LPS
  transport, compromises the outer-membrane permeability barrier and arrests
  growth.

- LptBFGC stoichiometry is 2:1:1:1 [PMID:20720015], so the LptC dimer seen on overexpression [PMID:21169485] is marked over-annotated.

- GO:0017089 -> MODIFY to GO:0140332 per current correct-but-general guidance; the P. putida LptC review makes the same refinement.
